vulnerabilities.description: Hardcoded demo credentials and plaintext sensitive data (workspace names, user names, budget info) exposed in demo data object. While marked as demo data, this creates a pattern for sensitive information exposure and could leak if this file is accidentally bundled into production.

Weak random ID generation fallback. Uses Math.random() and Date.now() as fallback when crypto.randomUUID() fails. Math.random() is not cryptographically secure and should never be used for session tokens.

Token injection via window variables (TOKEN, PORT) without visible validation. If the server doesn't properly escape these values when injecting them, this could be vulnerable to script injection attacks.
localStorage usage without encryption for session state. Sensitive session data is stored in plain localStorage, which is readable by any script on the same origin. No encryption is applied.
Unsafe JSON.parse() without try-catch validation depth. While wrapped in try-catch, malicious JSON payloads could cause denial-of-service through prototype pollution or large object creation.
No visible Content Security Policy or XSS protection headers configured in the provided linting/build config files. CSP should be enforced at the server/worker level.

recommendations: Move all demo credentials and sensitive data into environment-only configuration files; never commit them to the repository even if marked as 'demo'.
Replace Math.random() fallback with a secure random generator or remove the fallback entirely, forcing crypto.randomUUID().
Implement server-side token validation and signing (e.g., JWT) for window.__IMPECCABLE_TOKEN__ injection to prevent tampering.
Encrypt session state before storing in localStorage, or use sessionStorage with same-origin-only settings.
Add Content Security Policy headers (worker level in Cloudflare Workers) to restrict script execution and prevent XSS.
Implement Subresource Integrity (SRI) checks for external scripts injected into pages.
Add JSON schema validation when parsing session data from localStorage to prevent prototype pollution.
Audit the Lovable MCP connection for secure secret management—verify that LOVABLE_API_KEY and other credentials are never logged or exposed.
Review build output files in `.output/` to ensure no secrets are included in minified/compiled code.
Enable TypeScript strict mode and @typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-call to catch unsafe operations.
